name: interactive-pdf-binder
description: Print-first navigation system for assembled multi-document PDF binders on US Letter (612x792pt, origin bottom-left). One component, three navigation surfaces: slip-sheet TOC cover, TOC entry (active/inactive), and a HOME return button stamped on every content page. Rendered by tool-pdf-interactive.py (reportlab + pypdf) — not a DOM component; html/css below describe the design-system preview surface.

variants.name: slip-sheet
variants.description: Generated TOC cover page preceding each source document: header title, org subtitle, 1.5pt rule, optional right-aligned draft label (first sheet only), italic footer instruction. Holds up to 8 TOC entries per sheet.

variants.name: toc-entry-inactive
variants.description: Navigable TOC row for a non-current document: navy number + title, invisible full-rect GoTo link to that document's slip sheet.

variants.name: toc-entry-active
variants.description: TOC row for the current document: grey-light highlight rect, black text, leading arrow indicator; no link (self).

variants.name: home-button
variants.description: 64x20pt navy rounded-rect (4pt radius) with white HOME label, lower-right placement. Stamped on every content page (never slip sheets); transparent GoTo link to page 0 top.

aria: PDF-native accessibility, not ARIA — navigation is /GoTo link annotations plus a PDF document outline (/PageMode /UseOutlines), with /DisplayDocTitle true. Source PDFs are not guaranteed to be tagged; Tagged-PDF reading-order conformance for assistive technology is an open accessibility question (see open_questions), not yet handled by the generator.

wcag.note: Print/PDF target. Contrast: navy #002e63 on white ~13:1 (AAA); white on navy ~13:1 (AAA). Keyboard/assistive-tech navigation depends entirely on source-PDF tagging, which the current generator does not add.

open_questions: oq-1: an earlier draft spec listed a 7th color GREY_MID (#666680, 'inactive entry subtitles') that does not exist in the canonical Python source (no subtitle rows are generated) — dropped from this recipe; confirm no production instance actually relies on it before treating this as fully closed.
oq-2: max 8 TOC entries per slip sheet is currently a hard limit in the generator — should this become a token, and how should binders with more than 8 documents paginate across multiple slip sheets?
oq-3: Tagged-PDF / reading-order conformance for assistive technology is currently unhandled — source PDFs pass through untagged.

oq-4: navy hex rounding — the RGB constant (0, 0.18, 0.39) computes to ~#002f63; the design draft and this recipe both state #002e63. Pin one value definitively against the live Python source constant.
